extracted.intended_audience: medical device manufacturers/applicants, hospital administrators, Medicare policy stakeholders, health care providers, and other stakeholders responding to CMS notice-and-comment
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed CMS criteria and procedures for (1) evaluating eligibility for New Technology Add-on Payments (NTAP) and OPPS device pass-through payments (including proposed repeal of the alternative pathway) and (2) constructing the FY2027 hospital wage index (data sources, inclusions/exclusions, verification, and geographic delineations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost criterion for new technology add-on payment (NTAP)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must provide cost information showing the technology is costly such that the DRG rate otherwise applicable to discharges involving the technology is inadequate (i.e., meets the cost criterion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes the maximum NTAP for a case involving the technology as 65% of the average cost of the technology (preliminary amounts listed for FY 2027 examples). CMS may update cost information in the final rule based on revised or additional information received. CMS invites public comment on whether each technology meets the cost criterion and its proposed NTAP amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newness period / determination of start date
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS determines the beginning of the 'newness period' for a technology based on the date the technology became commercially available or the date it received FDA marketing authorization, as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each device example CMS states the specific date it considers the newness period to commence (e.g., date it became commercially available or received FDA marketing authorization). CMS requests confirmation of first U.S. availability dates when applicants report delayed availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three statutory NTAP eligibility criteria (§412.87(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning with FY 2028 applications, all applicants must meet the three criteria in §412.87(b): (1) the medical service or technology must be new; (2) it must be costly such that the DRG rate is inadequate; and (3) it must demonstrate a substantial clinical improvement over existing services or technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes to require all applicants (including FDA Breakthrough Devices, QIDPs, and LPAD drugs) to meet all three criteria rather than be eligible under an alternative pathway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial clinical improvement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A technology must represent an advance that substantially improves, relative to technologies previously available, the diagnosis or treatment of Medicare beneficiaries (i.e., demonstrate substantial clinical improvement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will evaluate substantial clinical improvement as part of the NTAP and OPPS pass-through determinations; applicants previously eligible under alternative pathways must now demonstrate this improvement. CMS provides opportunities (e.g., New Technology Town Hall) to present on the substantial clinical improvement criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal of alternative pathway for Breakthrough/QIDP/LPAD
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to repeal the alternative inpatient NTAP and OPPS device pass-through payment pathway that exempted FDA-designated Breakthrough Devices, QIDPs, and LPAD-approved drugs from the requirement to demonstrate substantial clinical improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications for FY 2028 and subsequent years (and OPPS applications on or after Oct 1, 2026) would be evaluated under the same standard as other applicants; technologies currently under review or previously approved under the alternative pathway remain eligible under the alternative pathway for FY 2027 and earlier approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA marketing authorization deadline for NTAP eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for consideration for the NTAP for the upcoming fiscal year (beginning with FY 2028 applications), applicants must have received FDA marketing authorization by May 1 of the year prior to the start of the fiscal year for which the application is being considered (§412.87(f)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS is also proposing to remove the conditional approval process that previously allowed some antimicrobial alternative-pathway applicants without timely FDA authorization to be conditionally approved (removal of §412.87(f)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: OPPS device pass-through substantial clinical improvement standard (§419.66(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: All OPPS device pass-through payment applications received on or after October 1, 2026 (with some transitional allowances) must demonstrate that the technology meets the device pass-through requirements, including showing a substantial clinical improvement under §419.66(c)(2)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications submitted as of September 30, 2026, for Breakthrough Devices that have marketing authorization may still be evaluated under the alternative pathway; CMS proposes to revise §419.66(c)(2)(ii) to reflect the policy effective Oct 1, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Device category code retention policy for pass-through payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Device category codes established based on approval (preliminary or final) would continue to be eligible for device pass-through payment status and remain in effect for at least 2 years but no more than 3 years (consistent with §419.66(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously existing device category codes that are no longer eligible would remain unchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to present at New Technology Town Hall
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for NTAP have an opportunity to present at the New Technology Town Hall Meeting on the substantial clinical improvement criterion for pending NTAP applications and have applications considered during annual IPPS rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS states this opportunity is part of ensuring that all applications undergo the same review process and that time to approval would not change for most applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that wage index updates be budget-neutral
rubrics_metrics.description: Any updates or adjustments to the hospital wage index must be made in a manner that ensures aggregate payments to hospitals are not affected by the change in the wage index (statutory requirement under section 1886(d)(3)(E)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will apply a budget neutrality adjustment when updating standardized amounts; the proposed adjustment for FY 2027 is described in the Addendum to the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor market area delineation using OMB Core-Based Statistical Areas (CBSAs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hospital labor market areas for assigning wage indexes are delineated based on OMB-established CBSAs and constituent county FIPS codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes to continue using the new OMB delineations released July 21, 2023 (OMB Bulletin No. 23-01) that were adopted beginning with FY 2025, and to continue to use FIPS county codes for crosswalking counties to CBSAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage index data reporting period (FY2023 cost reports) for FY2027 wage index
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed FY 2027 wage index values are based on Medicare cost report data from cost reporting periods beginning in FY 2023 (begin date on or after Oct 1, 2022 and before Oct 1, 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS refers to these as 'FY 2023 cost report'/'FY 2023 wage data'; the data file used was the FY 2023 data submitted as of January 21, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage index inclusions (types of costs/hours included)
rubrics_metrics.description: Included data categories: salaries and hours from short-term acute care hospitals (including paid lunch hours and hours associated with military leave and jury duty); home office costs and hours; certain contract labor costs and hours (direct patient care including nursing, certain top management, pharmacy, laboratory, nonteaching physician Part A services, certain contract indirect patient care services); and wage-related costs including pension costs and other deferred compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS cites prior final rules that established or modified treatment of these categories (FY 2008, FY 2012, FY 2016 rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage index exclusions (types of costs/hours excluded)
rubrics_metrics.description: Excluded from the wage index: direct and overhead salaries and hours for services not subject to IPPS payment (e.g., SNF services, home health services), costs related to GME (teaching physicians and residents), CRNAs, subprovider components not paid under IPPS, hospital-based RHCs and FQHCs, CAHs, REHs, and certain other wage-related costs (Worksheet S-3 Part II Line 18, Part IV Line 25 and subscripts, and contract labor costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS references prior rules (FY 2004, FY 2008, FY 2019, FY 2015) as the basis for these exclusions and explains rationale (e.g., CAHs distort area wage indexes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupational mix data collection requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(d)(3)(E) provides for collection of data every 3 years on the occupational mix of employees for short-term acute care hospitals to construct an occupational mix adjustment to the wage index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS references OMB control number for the information collection and plans to apply the occupational mix adjustment as discussed in section III.E of the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification and handling of aberrant wage data
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS reviews wage data to identify and resolve aberrant data; for FY 2027 CMS identified and excluded 68 providers with aberrant data and adjusted certain aberrant data (e.g., imputed estimates where hospitals lacked documentable salaries/hours for housekeeping and dietary services).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS did not subject FY 2023 wage data to a MAC desk review for FY 2027; instructed MACs to transmit changes by March 21, 2026; included FY 2023 data submitted as of Jan 21, 2026; if some excluded providers' data are corrected, CMS intends to include them in the final wage index. Imputation is performed consistent with policies established in the FY 2015 final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of data from hospitals that were IPPS in FY2023
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS will include wage data for facilities that were IPPS hospitals in FY 2023 even if they have since terminated participation, provided their data do not fail CMS reasonableness edits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows use of historical FY 2023 cost report data even if hospital status changed after that reporting period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of wage index data by other providers/suppliers
rubrics_metrics.description: IPPS wage index data are used to calculate wage indexes applicable to other suppliers/providers (SNFs, HHAs, ASCs, hospices) and for prospective payments to IRFs, IPFs, LTCHs, and hospital outpatient services; however, CMS will not address comments on other supplier/provider wage indexes in IPPS rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments about wage indexes for non-IPPS suppliers/providers should be made in response to separate proposed rules for those sectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment and solicitation of alternative methods
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS invites public comment on its proposals (e.g., whether specific technologies meet NTAP cost or clinical criteria, and on the proposal to require all applicants to meet the same eligibility standards) and asks for information on alternative methods stakeholders believe would better align payment with value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS is specifically interested in suggestions for alternative strategies for leveraging FDA designations and other ways to facilitate payment for innovative, high-value technologies that demonstrate improved beneficiary outcomes.
